name: Swiss Institute
funding: Pro Helvetia, NYSCA and NYC Cultural Affairs (2025-26); Warhol, Arison Arts, Frankenthaler, LUMA and Goldsmith foundations. Blavatnik Family Foundation gave in 2020 and 2021, Bloomberg Philanthropies in 2018 and 2019.
watch: Bloomberg (2018-19) and Blavatnik Family Foundation (2020-21) were partners; neither is listed since, so neither is a current funder.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, partners are named by year from 2018 to 2026, and the board is listed.

name: The Kitchen
funding: Mellon gave $2M in 2023. Its About page thanks Bloomberg Philanthropies as a supporter. FY2025 revenue was $2.4M, of which $2.1M was contributions, against $3.4M expenses.
watch: Experimental non-profit performance and media arts center founded in 1971.
why_flagged: Bloomberg Philanthropies is campaigned against elsewhere, not at The Kitchen. Robert Soros chairs the board.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, supporters appear only as undated logos without names, and the board is listed.

name: MASS MoCA
funding: Massachusetts Cultural Council, Barr Foundation, NEA, admissions and individual philanthropy.
records_note: It posts no reports or accounts; ProPublica holds its Form 990s for 2001 to 2025, two funder logos sit in the footer, trustees are listed.

name: Nottingham Contemporary
funding: Arts Council England is principal funder. Headline supporters include Bloomberg Philanthropies and the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation (UK Branch); Nottingham City Council, two universities and trusts also give.
watch: Calouste Gulbenkian's oil fortune counts as fossil-fuel money. In July 2020, 25 current and former staff sent an open letter to its leadership.
records_note: Names supporters by tier with no date and lists ten board members; no annual reports posted, accounts for 2021 to 2025 sit on the register.

name: Oakville Galleries
funding: Canada Council, Ontario Arts Council, Government of Ontario, Town of Oakville, Mondriaan Fund. Sponsors: Hatch, Taglieri Group, Siemens, Chatsworth Fine Homes.
watch: Siemens kept its Carmichael coal-mine rail contract in January 2020 despite protests. Woodbine racetrack gave an auction item; TD is not listed.
records_note: Names sponsors, donors and foundations on its funding page and lists its board, but links no annual reports or financial statements.

name: Bemis Center
funding: Sponsor page, $20,000+ tier: Mellon, Art Bridges, NEA, Nebraska Arts Council, Sherwood, Holland, Heider and Hubbard foundations, Douglas County, National Indemnity, Omaha Steaks. 2024 expenses $2.4M.
watch: Non-profit artist residency and contemporary gallery in Omaha.
records_note: No annual reports found; 990s are on ProPublica, the sponsorship page names donors by tier without a date, and the board is listed.

name: Astrup Fearnley Museet
funding: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality, the Thomas Fearnley, Heddy and Nils Astrup and Hans Rasmus Astrup foundations, and Sparebankstiftelsen DNB; sponsors EGD Holding and The Thief.
watch: Corporate Underwritten: Major private museum on Oslo's waterfront founded by shipping magnate Hans Rasmus Astrup. Core endowment derived from historic global shipping and offshore maritime logistics; adheres to Norwegian foundation oversight.
why_flagged: Norwegian Ministry of Culture and Equality, the Thomas Fearnley, Heddy and Nils Astrup and Hans Rasmus Astrup foundations, and Sparebankstiftelsen DNB; sponsors EGD Holding and The Thief.
records_note: The museum posts no annual report, but its accounts are in Norway's register, its board is named and funders and sponsors are listed undated.

name: Kröller-Müller Museum
funding: The Ministry of OCW, VriendenLoterij and the Helene Kröller-Müller Fonds are named in the site footer.
watch: Autonomous national museum within De Hoge Veluwe national park. Does not permit corporate commercial branding inside historic sculpture galleries; funded by state subsidies and historic philanthropic endowment.
records_note: The museum posts annual reports with accounts for 2017 to 2025, names its supervisory board, and names its main funders in the 2025 report.

name: Modern Art Oxford
funding: £3.1M income (FY2025). Arts Council England £909k a year, Oxford City Council £50k; Wolfson, Garfield Weston, Fidelity and other trusts; Lavazza, Edel Assanti, law firms, Oxford Brookes.
watch: No protest, boycott or flagged funder found. Oxford City Council cut its grant from £70k to £50k.
records_note: No annual reports found; accounts are on the Charity Commission register, the support page names capital funders undated, and trustees are listed.

name: Fondation Cartier
funding: Created in 1984 by Cartier SA and funded by Cartier, part of Richemont. Moved to a new Jean Nouvel site at the Palais-Royal, reopening 25 October 2025.
watch: High-calibre architectural commissions and curatorial programming funded directly through luxury jeweler Cartier / Richemont corporate balance sheet.
why_flagged: In 2023 Yanomami leaders and anthropologist Bruce Albert criticised Cartier's greenwashing use of a Yanomami photo. Cartier removed it and called it an oversight.
records_note: No annual report, accounts, funder list or board is posted; the site names its founder, a president and a managing director only.

name: Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature
funding: Private museum run by the public-interest Fondation François Sommer, set up by François and Jacqueline Sommer. A Friends association funds acquisitions.
watch: Established in 1964 by philanthropic benefactors François and Jacqueline Sommer. Operates independently from commercial corporate sponsorship, with an endowment focused on biodiversity and ecological conservation.
records_note: Neither the museum nor Fondation François Sommer posts annual reports, accounts, a donor list or its board; only the Friends association names its own directors.

name: Palais de Tokyo
funding: French state, plus patrons: Fondation Engie, Richard Mille, Ruinart, Swiss Life, Matmut, Revolut, Hugo Boss, G7. Exhibition partners include Havaianas and Vlisco.
watch: Fondation Engie is named in the footer as annual supporter and in the Sustainable Palais programme. Engie sells gas.
why_flagged: French state, plus patrons: Fondation Engie, Richard Mille, Ruinart, Swiss Life, Matmut, Revolut, Hugo Boss, G7. Exhibition partners include Havaianas and Vlisco.
records_note: It posts activity reports for 2020 to 2025 off its main menu, naming its board and 2025 supporters, with budget totals but no full accounts.
